title: Ansel and the Garden
premise: Jonah Ravensworth, exiled to the magic-dead valley of Hollowmere for a storm-calling that killed her family, has spent ten years tending a garden and pretending the world beyond the ridge doesn't exist. When prayers begin reaching the old gods again and a dying messenger begs her to unbind King Aldric from the crown-spirit devouring him, Jonah must cross into a world where her forbidden power answers every heartbeat. Guided by a disgraced god's last priest and a runaway royal ward who becomes the family she never chose, she learns the crown-spirit is one of the old gods herself—starved and mad from centuries of unanswered prayer. In the end, Jonah cannot kill the god without becoming her vessel; instead she offers the storm she swore never to call, unbinding the king at the cost of her exile's safety, and chooses to stay in the broken world with her found family rather than retreat to the valley.
about_author: Rosalind Coldharbour is the pen name of a former botanist who traded field notebooks for fantasy manuscripts after a decade cataloguing alpine wildflowers. She writes about exile, gardens, and gods from a stone cottage she insists has no ghosts.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Establishes Hollowmere's silence: no spells cross the ridge, and Jonah's storm-calling lies dormant under her skin like scar tissue. She tends her garden, trades herbs, avoids the village children who whisper about the Ravensworth curse. Emotional beat: the ache of chosen smallness.

chapters.title: A Prayer With No Address
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A stranger collapses at her gate—a courier carrying a sealed plea for the old gods, addressed to 'anyone still listening.' Inside the valley it should be inert paper; instead it hums against Jonah's skin. Emotional beat: dread as the dead valley stirs for the first time in ten years.

chapters.title: What the Ridge Remembers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The courier dies of wounds taken on the road, whispering that the king is 'wearing something hungry.' Jonah climbs the ridge at night and feels, for the first time since exile, the faint pressure of magic waiting on the other side. Emotional beat: terror and longing braided together.

chapters.title: The Priest Who Buried His God
chapters.summary: Bram's POV introduced. Bram Ostell, last priest of the forgotten god Veyra, arrives hunting the same courier, expecting a rival zealot and finding a gardener instead. He recognizes what Jonah is by the frost on her windowpanes. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two people hiding from their pasts.

chapters.title: Terms of Exile
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Flashback woven through present argument: the storm she called at fourteen, the family it buried, the council that spared her only because the valley could hold her. Bram argues the crown-spirit will eventually reach even Hollowmere. Emotional beat: guilt weaponized against hope.

chapters.title: The Ward Who Stole a Horse
chapters.summary: Sef's POV introduced. Sef, twelve-year-old royal ward, flees the capital disguised as a stable boy, carrying proof that the king's edicts are being written in a hand that isn't his. She crosses paths with Bram and Jonah at a border shrine. Emotional beat: ferocious self-reliance masking fear.

chapters.title: Three Strangers, One Road
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. The trio grudgingly travels together toward the capital; Sef picks pockets, Bram prays to nothing, Jonah flinches from every thundercloud. First sign the crown-spirit knows they're coming: birds fall silent along the whole road. Emotional beat: the fragile first stitches of found family.

chapters.title: The God Who Answers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At a ruined chapel, Jonah's suppressed magic surges when she touches the altar—the old gods really are waking, and her storm-calling is a key they recognize. She nearly levels the chapel. Emotional beat: horror at discovering her power was never gone, only leashed.

chapters.title: Crown and Cage
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. Inside the palace, Aldric fights moments of clarity between the crown-spirit's possessions, hiding notes to himself in his own handwriting. He remembers ordering the courier sent—and why he chose Jonah Ravensworth specifically. Emotional beat: dignity eroding into desperation.

chapters.title: The City That Prays Too Loud
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The trio enters the capital, where mass hysteria blooms: shrines overflow, cults brawl, and the crown-spirit feeds on desperate worship. Sef uses her knowledge of servant passages to hide them in the palace undercroft. Emotional beat: awe curdling into revulsion at weaponized faith.

chapters.title: What Wears the King
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. First confrontation with possessed Aldric; the crown-spirit speaks through him, calling Jonah 'little weather' and revealing it knew her family. It offers to return her dead if she kneels. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened into a blade.

chapters.title: Veyra's Last Secret
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram confesses his god Veyra didn't die—she was bound into the crown generations ago by priests trying to cage her hunger, and his order's true sin was abandonment. The crown-spirit is a starving god, not a demon. Emotional beat: shame transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: The Garden Beneath the Palace
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Hiding in the abandoned royal conservatory, Sef and Jonah tend dying plants together; Jonah teaches her grafting, and Sef teaches her that running isn't the same as surviving. They find records proving Aldric once tried to free himself. Emotional beat: quiet domesticity as an act of defiance.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. A palace informant sells their location; Bram is captured buying them time to escape, and the crown-spirit interrogates him through Aldric's mouth. Jonah must choose rescue over the ritual window. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against the mission.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Spire
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah calls a controlled storm for the first time in ten years to breach the spire prison—deliberately, precisely, nothing like the storm that killed her family. She frees Bram but the effort marks her visibly as a storm-caller to every watching eye. Emotional beat: reclamation shadowed by exposure.

chapters.title: The Council of Ash
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The ruling council, half-possessed already, brands Jonah an enemy of the realm; Sef reveals her identity as the king's ward to force an audience, gambling her life on Aldric's buried self hearing her. Emotional beat: courage as a wager with no sure odds.

chapters.title: Two Kings, One Crown
chapters.summary: King Aldric's POV. In a lucid hour engineered by Sef's presence, Aldric gives Jonah the ritual of unbinding—and asks her to let him die if the binding fails, rather than live as the god's puppet. Emotional beat: the terrible gift of being trusted with someone's ending.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Climax begins: in the throne room before the assembled court, Jonah begins the ritual while the crown-spirit floods the hall with worshippers' borrowed devotion. Bram holds the liturgy, Sef guards Aldric's body. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Little Weather
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The crown-spirit abandons Aldric and seizes Jonah, offering her the storm-godhood she was born for; inside the vision she relives her family's deaths and finally forgives the child who called the lightning. Emotional beat: the darkest hour and the turn.

chapters.title: An Answer at Last
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Instead of destroying the starving god, Jonah answers her centuries of unanswered prayer—offering her own storm freely given, which no binding can hold. The crown shatters; Veyra dissolves into rain over the city; Aldric breathes free. Emotional beat: compassion as the ultimate act of power.

chapters.title: After the Rain
chapters.summary: Rotating POV. Aftermath: Aldric, diminished but human, reforms the council; Bram rebuilds Veyra's faith around listening rather than asking; Sef refuses to return to being a ward and claims her place as the king's adopted daughter. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude sharing a table.

chapters.title: Seeds Carried Over the Ridge
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah returns to Hollowmere—not to hide, but to bring word, seeds, and letters, keeping a garden in both worlds now. Magic follows her gently across the ridge, and this time she lets it. Final emotional beat: home redefined as people, not walls.
